inputs.root_cause: ORA-DOCUMENT-001's three obligations required_tests: 'Root/canvas/profile boundary and overflow matrices; model construction without I/O.' model/document.py's OraDocument (width/height/version/root/xres/yres) already existed and codec/stack_xml.py's parse_stack() already enforced every domain invariant (positive w/h, required version, xres/yres specified together and defaulting to 72, positive resolution) at parse time -- but OraDocument had no __post_init__ of its own. A caller constructing or editing an OraDocument directly, bypassing the XML parser, could build an invalid document (negative width, empty version, non-positive xres) with no refusal. model/stack.py's OraNode already established the precedent for this exact situation: its own docstring states 'reject invalid values without altering the document applies to construction, not only to XML parsing... the same domain checks codec/stack_xml.py applies while parsing apply here too', enforced via __post_init__ so dataclasses.replace()-based editing is held to it too.

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed ora's remaining partial capabilities after ORA-MIMETYPE-001 (this session's prior slice), looking for another obligation where existing code was already complete but under-tested/mis-cited. ORA-DOCUMENT-001 (3 obligations, all sharing 'Root/canvas/profile boundary and overflow matrices; model construction without I/O' as required_tests) stood out: model/document.py's own module docstring literally quotes two of the three obligations' exact normative text, a strong signal the model was already built to match them.

2. Read model/document.py: OraDocument was a plain frozen dataclass with zero validation of its own -- every invariant lived in codec/stack_xml.py's parse_stack(). Confirmed via grep that OraDocument(...) is constructed at exactly one call site in the shipped namespace (parse_stack), meaning the model's own invariants were, in practice, enforced only accidentally by that single caller always passing already-validated values -- not because the model itself required it.

3. Read model/stack.py's OraNode.__post_init__ and its docstring in full: it establishes the exact precedent this obligation needs -- domain invariants belong in __post_init__, not only the parser, specifically so dataclasses.replace()-based editing (which re-runs __init__/__post_init__) is held to the same rules as initial construction.

4. Added OraDocument.__post_init__ (model/document.py): positive width/height/xres/yres via a new _require_positive helper, non-empty version. Deliberately did NOT re-validate 'xres and yres specified together' at the model level -- once constructed, xres/yres are always both present (defaulted to 72), so there is no absent/present distinction left for the model to check; that clause is inherently about the XML wire form parse_stack reads, already covered by existing parser-level tests. Deliberately did NOT move the canvas-area overflow check (checked_product against a caller's resource budget) into the model either -- that is a resource-limit concern requiring a ResourceLimits object the dataclass constructor does not have, correctly scoped to codec/stack_xml.py.

5. Ran the full ORA suite before writing any new tests to confirm the new __post_init__ introduced zero regressions: 261 passed, unchanged (parse_stack already only ever passes valid values through, so the new checks are a no-op on every existing call path).

6. Wrote tests/python/ora/test_obligation_document_model_construction.py (14 tests): direct OraDocument(...) construction with valid values (no XML involved), explicit-resolution retention, pixel_count availability immediately after construction, one negative test per invariant (width/height/version/xres/yres) proving direct construction refuses invalid values with a diagnostic naming the field, and two dataclasses.replace() tests proving editing is refused the same way and that replace() produces an independent object.
7. All 14 passed on first run. Re-ran the full ORA suite: 275 passed (261 baseline + 14 new, 0 regressions). ruff and mypy clean on the full package (13 source files).

8. Corrected all three obligations' source_symbols/positive/negative selectors to their own precise, differentiated set (the w/h/version obligation, the full-typed-exposure-plus-overflow obligation, and the resolution-specific obligation each cite a distinct, overlapping-but-not-identical subset) and promoted all three to implemented.

evidence.why_this_is_real_new_code_not_pure_citat: Unlike the prior ORA-MIMETYPE-001 slice (0 source changes), this one required a genuine, if small, source change: OraDocument had no __post_init__ before this slice, and the obligation's own required_tests explicitly names 'model construction without I/O' as something to prove -- which was not actually true until this slice added the validation that makes it true.
